en: When you hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning, so you must immediately seek shelter indoors.
Washing your hands with soap after touching soil prevents harmful bacteria and parasites from entering your body through small cuts.
Boiling floodwater for at least one minute kills harmful bacteria, making it safe to drink during severe typhoons.
Wearing thick rubber shoes protects your feet from sharp, glass-like volcanic rocks like obsidian when hiking on trails.
The Sun emits ultraviolet rays that cause sunburns, so you must apply sunscreen to protect your skin outdoors.
During an earthquake, dropping to the ground and covering your head under a sturdy table prevents injuries from falling debris.
Strong ocean currents driven by the Moon's gravity can sweep swimmers away, so always swim near a lifeguard.
Drinking plenty of water and resting in the shade prevents heatstroke when extreme summer temperatures cause dangerous heatwaves.
Locating the North Star, Polaris, helps you determine true north and avoid getting lost when hiking at night.
Avoiding wading in floodwaters prevents leptospirosis, a severe bacterial infection spread through the urine of infected rats.
Damp, rainy weather promotes indoor mold growth, which can trigger asthma attacks and allergic reactions in children.
If ocean water suddenly recedes from the shore after an earthquake, it signals an incoming tsunami, so evacuate immediately.
